title: Intuit deepens its investment in India with the opening of its new Bengaluru campus
summary: Intuit has opened a new Bengaluru campus, bringing together engineering, product, platform, and AI teams to accelerate innovation and strengthen India’s role as a global technology hub.

- [All Posts](https://www.intuit.com/blog/all-posts/)


- [Global Stories](https://www.intuit.com/blog/hub/global-stories/)


- Intuit deepens its investment in India with the opening of its new Bengaluru campus


Today, Intuit announced the opening of our new campus at Embassy Tech Village on Outer Ring Road in Bellandur, Bengaluru. The two-tower campus brings Intuit India’s teams together in one place. By expanding our footprint, Intuit India is the company’s second-largest engineering center globally. It is designed to enable seamless collaboration and innovation with greater velocity. Intuit has a strong belief that when engineers, product teams, and designers work side by side, it’s easier to turn big ideas into better customer experiences, and strengthen our builder culture.


The campus reflects Intuit’s global workplace strategy: to attract and retain top talent around the world and enable them to do the best work of their lives. With a hybrid working model in place, we’re continuing to invest in modern, best-in-class workplaces that foster connection, belonging and spark creativity. These spaces also reflect our commitment to sustainability and our goal of reaching net-zero greenhouse gas emissions across our operations and supply chain by FY40.


## **A campus that feels like Bengaluru**


*“We wanted a campus that feels like Bengaluru, with local art, craftsmanship, and character woven throughout, while supporting the kind of world-class innovation our teams deliver every day. This campus is about bringing top tech talent together to write Intuit’s next chapter of growth and innovation in India. I’m proud of what our teams have built, and excited for what they’ll create here,” said Saurabh Saxena, senior vice president and India site lead at Intuit.*


The local touches begin the moment visitors arrive. Our values greet guests with hand-painted art from Kala Kart, a local truck artist, and the lobby, named Garden City | Namma Ooru (“our city” in Kannada), draws inspiration from Bengaluru’s gardens. In the stairwells, a graphic traces a Bengaluru bus route from floor to floor. Each floor is themed around a customer industry we serve, with murals and installations by Indian artists, so our teams are surrounded by the businesses they build for. The Bangalore Bungalow, a meeting room, reimagines the kitchen table where Intuit’s story began, where co-founder Scott Cook watched his wife struggle to balance the checkbook and thought, ‘There must be a better way.’


### **Innovation for customers around the world**


The campus reflects India’s role as a key technology and innovation hub for Intuit, and our continued investment in the people and ideas shaping the future of AI and finance. Nearly a quarter of Intuit’s global technology talent is based in Bengaluru, where we’ve had teams since 2005. Those teams build our platform, products, and AI-driven experiences that power prosperity for consumers, businesses, and accountants around the world.


*“Our teams in Bengaluru are central to how we build the AI-driven experiences that help our customers prosper,” said Alex Balazs, chief technology officer at Intuit. “This campus gives them a place to do their best work, and it’s a home for the innovation they build to bring financial intelligence to customers around the world.”*


The new campus celebrates the engineers who build globally scalable technology, the product teams who solve real customer problems, the designers who turn bold ideas into working solutions, and the local businesses and artists who helped bring this vibrant workplace to life. It reinforces our commitment to driving global AI innovation from India.
